rows: Isolate the direct supply switch of the sensor from the panel next to the sampling instrument
Isolate the power from the main supply source
Remove the socket from the upper base of the instrument
Remove the instrument from the lower base and take it to the laboratory for maintenance
Dismantle the upper part of the sensor, which consists of two parts (a lead coil representing the anode and the other part is the platinum tip representing the cathode)
Clean the sensor thoroughly of oxidation and accumulated rust
Clean the inner vessel of the sensor thoroughly of adhering deposits
Check the integrity and accuracy of the insulation (Teflon membrane), which insulates the water from the electrode and can be replaced if damaged
Return the sensor to its place on site and reconnect it
Reconnect the main power switch as well as the direct supply switch

Check that the sensor is operating normally by bringing water with a known oxygen (O2) content and comparing the reading shown on the indicator with the known value; if the two readings differ, readjust the indicator to the known value in coordination with the Chemistry Department, and if adjustment is not possible, replace the sensor or the indicator, whichever is faulty

This document sets out the calibration steps
This instrument is used to measure the dissolved oxygen content of boiler water. There are 8 identical instruments, one for each boiler.
The first draft of this document was prepared by Eng. Wagdy Eid Mansour and Eng. Amal Hamed El-Maken, reviewed by Eng. Taher Abdel Galil Mohamed Mostafa El-Khatib, tested by Eng. Doaa Mohamed Shabana, approved by the General Manager Eng. Yousry Ahmed Abdel Maksoud, reviewed by Eng. Abdel Monem El-Emam, Manager of the Instrumentation and Electricity Department in the Inspection Sector of the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company, and approved by Eng. Fathy Mahmoud Ragab, Head of the Talkha Power Station Sector.
It was approved by Eng. Samir Abdel Galil, General Manager of Inspection and Quality of the East Delta Electricity Production Company and MPIS Coordinator, and approved by Mr. Accountant Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman, General Manager of Financial and Administrative Control and Supervisor of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector.
Safety Precautions
Issue a work permit, with an industrial safety category card available for the personnel on site
Fence off the area, using the appropriate warning signs
Use personal protective equipment (PPE) such as a safety helmet and safety shoes, etc.

Procedures to be Carried Out
Isolate the direct supply switch of the sensor from the panel next to the sampling instrument | 1.
Isolate the power from the main supply source | 2.
Remove the socket from the upper base of the instrument | 3.
Instrument maintenance:
Remove the instrument from the lower base and take it to the laboratory for maintenance | 1.
Dismantle the upper part of the sensor, which consists of two parts (a lead coil representing the anode and the other part is the platinum tip representing the cathode) | 2.
Clean the sensor thoroughly of oxidation and accumulated rust | 3.
Clean the inner vessel of the sensor thoroughly of adhering deposits | 4.
Check the socket connection terminals | 5.
Check the integrity and accuracy of the insulation (Teflon membrane), which insulates the water from the electrode and can be replaced if damaged | 6.
Reassemble the above parts | 7.
Return the sensor to its place on site and reconnect it | 8.
Reconnect the main power switch as well as the direct supply switch | 9.
Check that the sensor is operating normally by bringing water with a known oxygen (O2) content and comparing the reading shown on the indicator with the known value; if the two readings differ, readjust the indicator to the known value in coordination with the Chemistry Department, and if adjustment is not possible, replace the sensor or the indicator, whichever is faulty | 10.
